title: FLOOD THE ZONE: Continue the Pressure for Transparency at Macon Water Authority
description:
Dear Neighbors and Community Leaders,

Our community STILL deserves answers. The ongoing issues surrounding the Macon Water Authority have raised serious concerns, and it’s time we come together and demand the transparency and accountability that every resident deserves.

The Macon-Bibb Democratic Committee is calling on you to stand with us at the next Macon Water Authority Committee Meeting. We are requesting  an audit of how our county funds are used and accessible meetings that are live-streamed to the public, as well as voicing opposition to ANY and ALL rate increases. 

We need a Water Authority that is proactive, not reactive. We not only need responses to emergencies, but also solid infrastructure that prevents unnecessary emergencies from happening in the first place.

We encourage everyone who believes in good governance and community power to show up. Together CONSISTENTLY, we can ensure that our concerns are heard and that real change follows. Let’s fill the room with unity, purpose, and the power of the people.

If you’re with us, sign the petition at https://www.change.org/p/demand-ethical-investigation-and-proper-management-at-macon-water-authority?recruiter=1371577776&recruited_by_id=c56cc790-1b8b-11f0-87a9-9dddcfc975b1&utm_source=share_petition&utm_campaign=petition_dashboard&utm_medium=copylink, and show up to Macon Water Authority on June 5th at 2PM and again at 4PM to FLOOD THE ZONE and let the board know that the citizens of Macon-Bibb are done being in the dark and we are holding them accountable.

In solidarity,

Renoalda Scott

Chair, Macon-Bibb Democratic Committee

title: Bethel Defends Democracy: Immigrant Rights
description:
Please join us for our 14th consecutive rally to Defend Democracy in beautiful downtown Bethel. While our overall theme is Defending Democracy, each week we pick a specific focus. On Saturday June 7th, 11am -12:30pm, our focus will be on Immigrant Rights.

“We lead the world because, unique among nations, we draw our people, our strength, from every country,  every corner of the world.”    

“ I believe in the idea of amnesty for those who have put down roots and who have lived here, even though sometime back, they may have entered illegally.”
       
Both of these quotes were made by 
             Ronald Reagan.

Immigrants in the United States, regardless of their immigration status, have certain rights guaranteed by the Constitution and federal laws. These include protection from discrimination, the right to due process, and the right to remain silent. Additionally, they have the right to legal representation, especially if detained or facing removal proceedings. 

Our guest speakers will be Juan Fonseca Tapia and Rachel Jordan.  

Juan will share his and other personal stories of what it's like to be an immigrant and what we can do to help our many friends and neighbors. He is a community organizer who also served in the United States Air Force Reserves. Juan immigrated to the U.S. from Mexico and has lived in Connecticut since 2012. He is one of the leaders of the local immigrant rights group, “Greater Danbury Area Unites for Immigrants”. 

Rachel is the managing attorney for policy and partnerships at a nonprofit legal services organization in NYC that provides free legal representation to unaccompanied immigrant children. She has been an attorney for immigrants’ rights and deportation defense since 2014, and is herself the proud daughter of a refugee. Though her family just made the move about 5 minutes away to Redding, she was born and raised in Bethel. 

Live music will be performed by one of our favorites, Dean Snellback from the local band Bluesyland.

The rally is non-partisian. All are welcome.

There will be something for everyone. We'll have speakers, we'll rally with our signs, we'll take a short march and we'll have live music. We also like to end each week with a sing-a-long.

A sign-making table will also be available, complete with all the necessary supplies, for young and old to make signs for the rally.

We also collect a non-perishable food item for our local food pantry each week. Anything you want to contribute is welcome, but some special requests from the food pantry include:

Spices, Coffee and Baking supplies are always needed.

Individually packaged items. so if you bought a variety pack of something like granola bars or instant oatmeal and discovered there's a flavor you won't eat, please give us the individual packs out of box.

Empty egg cartons- Any style, so long as they're clean.

SMALL empty detergent bottles

Note: Rally is rain or shine.

There are 2 small benches at the square and we will have a limited number of camping chairs. Please bring your own lawn or camping chair if you'd like.

Approximate Rally Schedule:

11:00 - 11:15 Assemble and rally at curb (You are welcome to arrive prior to 11:00 for extra curb time)

11:15 - 11:45 Speaker(s)

11:45 - Noon Rally at curb with chant leader

Noon - 12:20 March with chant leader

12:20   Closing Song

12:30   Disperse

We ask that attendees refrain from sign holding or chanting at the curb during our speaking portion of the rally. We have had issues with speakers being heard because of the increased honking. It also is a courtesy to the speakers who are often discussing serious and sensitive topics. We are sharing a small square so we need your help to make the rallies comfortable for everyone.

We have tried to arrange the rallies so there is a little something for everyone: chanting, marching, themes with speakers, live music, fun trinkets, sign making. We appreciate every one of you that attends and we are working hard to bring all of us together to voice our frustrations, build community and also hopefully learn a little something from experts or your fellow neighbors experiences.

We appreciate your understanding and cooperation. ❤️

We also ask that you park at one of the four public parking lots. The lot that is very close to the rally location, PT Barnum Square, is behind the municipal center (number 1 on the map you will receive after registration). PT Barnum Square is the triangle shaped area to the far right on the map and in the center of the map.

Although all street parking is public, we ask that you please not park in the limited parking spots in front of our local businesses, but definitely enjoy our beautiful towns restaurants and shops after the rally! 
Thank you 😊

title: Sign the Petition for SB1 Referendum at Blufton Farmers Market
description:
We'll be at the Blufton Farmers Market this Saturday from 8am-12pm to collect signatures for the SB1 Referendum. If it rains, the petition table will be inside Twisted Whisk.

WHAT IS SENATE BILL 1?
-Senate Bill 1 (“The Higher Education Destruction Act”) was signed into OH law by Gov. DeWine on March 28, 2025 and goes into effect on June 25, 2025. 
-SB1 guts collective bargaining rights for faculty unions, removes job protections for educators & bans striking time for full-time staff.
-SB1 allows colleges & universities to end programs & terminate faculty positions without warning or cause.
-SB1 bans most diversity, equity & inclusion programs and staff training in higher education.
-We have until June 22 to collect 250,000 signatures in OH and get a repeal measure on the Nov. ballot.
-Republicans in OH leadership have now introduced bills (SB113 & HB155) targeted at grades K-12. We must stop attacks on public education!
-For more information, visit ohiosb1petition.com
-Sign the petition to repeal SB1!
